thought: He lost his right arm at five. At the Commonwealth Games, he ran the 100m faster than anyone in the field ever had.
support: Dilip Gavit grew up in a farming family near Nashik. An untreated childhood injury cost him his forearm - it didn't cost him the sport. He set a Commonwealth Games record in the T47 100m, and a fellow Indian took silver behind him. The record only measures the race. It doesn't measure how long the road to the start line was.
